The twins Ma'te and Lo'te had saved him then forsaking the safety and security of the Burrows to lead their people out in the wilds of the forest. Their dedication had given him the strength to rally and reforge the severed bonds of his kin. Peace had returned to his tribe for a time and so it stayed until the Gods wrath fell upon them and stole the light from his life.

Me'le, his wife had always maintained her faith in the Gods even in their darkest moments when the walls of the Burrows had trembled all around them "Yuna will provide" She had said, her calm voice and stoic demeanor soothing the king's fears and giving him the strength to continue even as the first tunnels began to fall.

He had begged her to come with him, to flee into the deepest caverns of the Burrows and the safety of stone, but the Queen had refused, her place, she said, was among her people providing support and aiding in the efforts to strengthen the tunnels against the tremors. He never got the chance to say goodbye, the earth had claimed her and countless numbers of their kin when the tunnels collapsed, a chance to mourn and recover their dead denied by the Gods continuous assault upon their home.

For the Chieftain this loss had been too great, his heart and mind pushed to its breaking point, abandoned by the Gods and with his council shattered Ma'Ten was all alone and in his isolation he fell to despair. Driven inward by his grief the Chieftain found only darkness, his mind drifting with only one wish, to save his people and to see his wife again. Within the darkness of his shattered spirit he found the magic of Umbralocht and other strange energies. With their touch was transformed, his mind warping into that of a tyrant, strong in will and stronger in spirit. For this new found power the Chieftain paid a terrible price for his soul was now so at odds with his mind that his psyche fractured and the man known as Ma'Ten was no more.

Unbidden and unconscious his will had flowed throughout the Burrows corrupting the minds of all it touched, only those with the strongest of wills had resisted unknowingly until time and fatigue had claimed them. In dreams and whispers the King's will drove them onwards ordering them never to tire nor hunger and by strange magics and unknown energies the Med'ja's bodies were fed, their minds descending into a spellbound stupor as their bodies drove ever onwards, slaves to the dark king's will.

The young of mammals have neotenous features: big eyes, big heads, round faces. Evolutionarily this is a survival mechanism: A species that finds its young disgusting would not be around for long. It makes the children "cute" and engenders feelings of love and protection from adults, especially from biologically related ones. However, kids aren't the only ones who have those features. Some females retain neotenous features into sexual maturity and adulthood. Think of it as a genetic mating strategy -- you retain the neotenous features into adulthood to piggyback onto the feelings of love and protection that a father has for his daughter. Due to co-evolution, males might in turn find neotenous features more sexually attractive in females. Evolution has a careful balancing act that it needs to maintain: Have men find those features sexually attractive in sexually mature females, but have the same features engender parental love and protection in non-sexually mature females.
